newsitem.title: UK: Morgan Stanley eyes Internet banking - paper.
newsitem.headline: Morgan Stanley eyes Internet banking - paper.

text.p: Morgan Stanley Dean Witter Discover & Co is considering a direct banking business over the Internet using the Discover credit card brand name, the Financial Times reported on Friday.

Philip Purcell, chairman of the recently merged U.S. investment banking, brokerage and credit card group, said in an interview with the newspaper that it was looking at using Discover to launch "something as radical as Discover Banking Direct".
The service would also include telephone banking.

"We like the Internet," Purcell said. "We think younger customers are going to be as comfortable with that as they are with the ATMs (automated teller machines)...It is a market segment which is going to do nothing but grow."
Last December, Dean Witter, Discover, as it was called then, became the first full-service brokerage to buy an Internet discount broker -- Lombard Brokerage.
Purcell said he hoped to launch the Discover card internationally in the next two years but security concerns were holding back the use of the Internet for credit card transactions.
